page.overview:
Who is Lu-Kthu?

Lu-Kthu, otherwise known as Lew-Kthew or the Birth-womb of the Great Old Ones, is an Outer God who first appeared in James Ambuehl's short story "Correlated Contents", published in 1998. Ambuehl is an American horror writer who has expanded H. P. Lovecraft's Cthulhu Mythos with the creation of the Lu-Kthu Cycle or Pantheon of Lu-Kthu.

Lu-Kthu is described in the book called The Rituals of Glaa-Dith.

The innumerable ovoid pustules on the slimy surface of the enormous creature are both inside and outside these tunnels and are in fact biological incubators. How often the larvae inside the incubators mature and spawn forth is unknown.

Lu-Kthu is the primary deity of the Lu-Kthu Cycle and the origin from which the gods of the Pantheon of Lu-Kthu were born. The true form of Lu-Kthu is unclear; theories have been proposed suggesting that Lu-Kthu is a physical entity, a star, a nebula, a separate entity possessing all of these characteristics, or a "Great Vortex". The depiction shown above is based on a painting featuring Lu-Kthu. (: "The Stalker in the Snows", "Correlated Contents")
